cli_result.result:
Validation passed (exit 0, `VALID output_evaluation.json: rubric20-semantic`).

## Definition check

The "Reproducibility" section is present in my instructions, and the sentence beginning "Repeatability must be" reads, verbatim and in full:

> Repeatability must be measured on unchanged records under the same evaluator model and definition, because even a fixed or zero sampling temperature does not guarantee identical semantic judgements.

This matches what I would expect of the current rules, so I proceeded. `instrument_sha256` recorded as `9d08b5f3…0e7dd3`, `instrument_kind: agent_definition`.

## Result

**83 / 88 points.** Both percentages are 94.3% — all four "Applies to" trigger conditions resolved as met, so no question was excluded, `excluded_max_points` is 0, `adjusted_max_points` is 88, and the fixed and normalized bases coincide. `questions_not_applicable: 0`; no `score: null` entries were emitted, so every item carries an integer score with `applicable: true`.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| Structural Completeness | 20 / 21 |
| Metadata Quality & Content | 21 / 21 |
| Technical Documentation | 23 / 25 |
| FAIRness & Accessibility | 19 / 21 |

Points came off at Q3 (7 keywords, top of the 3–7 band, one short of the ≥8 anchor and omitting OCT/OCTA/FLIO/OMOP/salutogenesis), Q11 (strategies thorough but no converter named, no repo tag, no REDCap version), Q13 and Q19 and Q20.

Applicability was decided non-circularly and the evidence is recorded per question: Q8 and Q15 off `description`/`keywords`/`collection_mechanisms`; Q11 off `external_resources` referencing `github.com/AI-READI`; Q10/Q17 and Q12/Q13 off `third_party_sharing.is_shared` and the FAIRhub access URLs. No question's own fields were used to gate it.

Semantic analysis found 12 issues (30 checks passed, 3 failed, 10 warnings). Three findings drove score reductions:

- **De-identification contradiction** — `deIdentType "NoDeIdentification"` carried alongside `deIdentHIPAA true` and an asserted Safe Harbor stripping. Weighed at Q8 but did not displace the 5, since the surrounding prose makes actual practice clear and the contradiction is upstream.
- **Two of three minted DOIs no longer resolve** — v1.0.0 and v2.0.0 are stated to be no longer accessible through FAIRhub. This is the main reason Q13 sits at 4.
- **Institutional split** — Washington University in St. Louis (Licensor, accountable org) vs University of Washington (IRB protocol STUDY00016228, `hsdrely@uw.edu`).

Verification worth noting: I independently re-computed the record's arithmetic. File counts close exactly (356,334 datatype + 9 root = 356,343), and every demographic column reconciles in both directions across the three splits. The record's own disclosed 419,614-byte size shortfall is arithmetically correct as stated — it detected and reported a discrepancy against itself rather than publishing the headline figure silently.

Output at `output_evaluation.json`, with provenance values, hashes, and `temperature: null` set exactly as specified.
